warmup/why: The learning rate does not have to stay fixed. Big steps make fast progress early on, and small steps settle in at the end.
warmup/ramp: Many runs begin with a warmup: the rate climbs in a straight line from zero to its peak, written eta max, over the first k steps. So at step t it is the peak times t over k.
warmup/ex: With a peak of zero point one over a thousand steps, step two hundred and fifty runs at a quarter of the peak: zero point zero two five.
warmup/reason: Why bother? At the start, far from any minimum, the slopes are steep and the gradients large. The full rate times a large gradient makes a huge step, which can overshoot and blow up, just as too large a rate does. So warmup eases in.
steps/rule: The classic decay goes in steps: multiply the rate by a factor, often zero point one, every so many steps.
steps/ex: Start at zero point one and drop every ten thousand steps: step fifteen thousand runs at zero point zero one, and step twenty-five thousand at zero point zero zero one.
steps/linear: Linear decay goes in a straight line instead, from the top rate, eta max, down to the bottom one, eta min, over T steps: the same drop every step. From zero point one to zero, sampled four times along the way: zero point zero seven five, zero point zero five, zero point zero two five, zero.
try/p1: Try one: the rate starts at zero point one and is multiplied by zero point one every five thousand steps. Counting steps from zero, what is the rate at step ten thousand?
try/a1: The drops come at steps five thousand and ten thousand, and step ten thousand is one of them. So two drops have happened: zero point one times zero point one, twice, is zero point zero zero one.
try/p2: Now linear decay from zero point one down to zero point zero one over a thousand steps. What is the rate at step four hundred?
try/a2: The gap is zero point zero nine. Four hundred of a thousand steps is zero point four of the way, so the rate has dropped zero point four times zero point zero nine: zero point zero three six. And zero point one minus zero point zero three six is zero point zero six four.
